{"body":"## Problem

The four CDK apps each carry their own `src/stacks/spa.stack.ts`:

- `apps/bacteria-game-remote-cdk/src/stacks/spa.stack.ts`, `apps/fourier-analysis-remote-cdk/…`, `apps/shader-examples-remote-cdk/…` — 16 LOC each. The fourier and shader files are **byte-identical**; the bacteria one differs only by `extraAllowedOrigins`/`noCacheFiles` pass-through.
- `apps/angular-examples-cdk/src/stacks/spa.stack.ts` (45 LOC) adds the shell-specific extra assets (wasm, `version.json`, federation manifests).

The shell's stack also needs this at line 3–4:

```ts
// eslint-disable-next-line @nx/enforce-module-boundaries
import { version } from '../../../../version.json';
```

This is the only `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries` suppression in `apps/` and `libs/`, and it is a stale `eslint-disable` (module boundaries now run through oxlint, so the comment does nothing) hiding a relative import that escapes the project root.

## Why it matters for modularity

Federated deployment config should be defined once. Three copies of the same stack mean a change to the SPA construct's props (CDN, cache headers) must be applied four times, and the root-escaping import is exactly the kind of cross-project reach the boundary rule exists to flag.

## Proposed change

1. Add a `createSpaStack`/`RemoteSpaStack` helper to `libs/public/spa-cdk-stack` **without touching its build targets** (new source file + barrel export only), or to a small `infra-shared` util; the three remote apps instantiate it, the shell extends it with its extra assets.
2. Replace the `version.json` import by passing the version in via `SpaProps` from each app's `main.ts` (or read it with `readFileSync` from `process.cwd()`), then delete the disable comment.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  shell[angular-examples-cdk] --> lib[spa-cdk-stack]
  r1[bacteria-game-remote-cdk] --> lib
  r2[fourier-analysis-remote-cdk] --> lib
  r3[shader-examples-remote-cdk] --> lib
```

## Effort

S

## Risk

Low. CDK snapshot tests exist for the construct; run `nx test spa-cdk-stack` and `nx run <app>-cdk:synth`/diff to confirm the synthesized template is unchanged. Note the target policy: `apps/*-cdk` keep `target: "ESNext"`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Only one definition of the plain remote SPA stack remains.
- [ ] No `eslint-disable … enforce-module-boundaries` comments left in `apps/` or `libs/`.
- [ ] Synthesized CloudFormation for all four stacks is unchanged.
- [ ] `libs/public/*` build targets untouched.

See [Automated findings](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/blob/main/docs/architecture/README.md#automated-findings).

content.text:
I've implemented issue #2483 and staged it on the new branch `refactor/cdk-shared-spa-stack` (cut from `origin/main`), but it isn't committed. The pre-commit hook failed because Nx can't build its project graph on this machine.

**What changed**
- **One shared stack:** `SpaStack` is now in [spa.stack.ts](libs/public/spa-cdk-stack/src/lib/spa/spa.stack.ts) in the library and exported from its index. It holds one `SpaConstruct` as `spa`. The build targets of `libs/public/*` are untouched.
- **Remotes:** I deleted the three copies of `spa.stack.ts`. The bacteria, fourier and shader `main.ts` files now import `SpaStack` from `@wolsok/spa-cdk-stack`.
- **Shell:** [angular-examples.stack.ts](apps/angular-examples-cdk/src/stacks/angular-examples.stack.ts) extends `SpaStack` and adds the wasm, `version.json` and federation files. It gets the version as a prop: [main.ts](apps/angular-examples-cdk/src/main.ts) reads `version.json` from `process.cwd()`. That is the workspace root, because the deploy tool runs from there. The import that reached outside the project and its suppression comment are gone. There are no `enforce-module-boundaries` suppressions left in `apps/` or `libs/`.
- **Library spec and README:** the spec now tests `SpaStack` directly instead of its own test copy, and the README has a short usage section.

**What I checked**
- **Templates:** I built the CloudFormation templates with the old and the new code and compared them. They are identical for the remote stack (19 resources) and the shell stack (21 resources). The four `main.ts` files themselves weren't synthesized, since that needs AWS credentials.
- **Tests:** all 8 library tests pass and the snapshots didn't change.
- **Format and types:** oxfmt is applied and `tsc` passes for all four CDK apps and the library.
- **Lint:** oxlint reports nothing, but its module-boundary rule was skipped because there was no project graph. CI will run it.
- **Already broken on `main`:** the spec has two `TS4111` type errors that exist there too. I left them alone.

**Why the commit is stuck:** SWC's native add-on refuses to load. Its error says the access rules on `C:\Users\Wolfr\AppData\Local` give "replacement rights" to an app-container ID (`S-1-15-3-…`). Without SWC, Nx can't build the project graph, so neither `nx test` nor the pre-commit hook runs, even outside my sandbox. I haven't changed those Windows permissions, since that's a security setting. You can fix it yourself, or I can commit with `--no-verify`, because the hook's checks were run by hand. After that I'll push, open the PR and request the CodeRabbit review.
